compare.ask: The food was cooked by my aunt.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “a festa foi planejada pela minha irmã” e “as luzes foram colocadas pelos meus primos”.
compare.tip: Diga: “The food was cooked by my aunt.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use was/were + particípio + by: The party was planned by my sister. The lights were put up by my cousins. Was é para uma coisa; were é para várias.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: The food was cooked by my aunt.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

facts.big: The party was planned by my sister
facts.label: Passivo no passado
facts.sub: Use was/were + particípio + by: The party was planned by my sister. The lights were put up by my cousins.

facts.label: foi / foram + particípio
facts.sub: Use was ou were com o particípio para falar do passado: The party was planned. The lights were put up. Was para um, were para vários.

facts.label: por + quem fez
facts.sub: Use by para dizer quem fez: planned by my sister, cooked by my aunt, chosen by my brother. Se a pessoa não importa, não precisa de by.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: The party was planned by my sister means my sister planned it.
We say “The lights was put up.”
items.why: Lights is plural: The lights were put up.

items.s: The passive in the past uses was/were + particípio.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: The party was planned by my sister means my sister planned it. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “The lights was put up.” → Falso (Lights is plural: The lights were put up.)
The passive in the past uses was/were + particípio. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A party room in Denver · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Saturday night in Denver. Abe stands at the door of a big party room. Soft music comes from the next room. Luisa arrives a little late. Everything looks perfect tonight. She wants to know who did all this.
“Welcome, Luisa! This party was planned by my sister.” says Abe. “It’s beautiful! Was the room cleaned by her too?” says Luisa. “Yes, and the lights were put up by my cousins.” says Abe.
